## Research Notes
See `research.md` (truth map). Key findings:
- `--mark` stdout has one consumer (`ledger.sh:820`, matching `not marked`), so a second `path:` line is safe.
- The re-hash (`ledger.sh:821-822`) currently follows the mark directly; with a commit in between it must
  move after the commit so a rolled-back mark leaves the stored hash matching the board (spec D4).
- `ledger.sh` is over the file limit → the new logic is a sourced `hooks/ledger-publish.sh`.
- Publish is already allowlisted for lanes (`hefesto-setup.sh:127`); no settings change.
- Two lanes publishing items in the same column file can race; a publish lock closes it.

## Data Model
Board config gains one optional key: `orchestrate.publish_commit` (boolean, default false). The ledger
entry is unchanged (`published` keeps its shape). No migration.

## API Contracts
- `status-board.sh --locate <id>` → exit 0, stdout `<column>\t<absolute resolved path>`; an item in DONE →
  `done\t-`; no item → non-zero (same message as `--mark`). Writes nothing.
- `status-board.sh --mark <id> <m>` → unchanged first line, plus `path: <absolute resolved path>` on success
  (no `path:` line for the DONE "not marked" case).
- `ledger.sh publish <id>` → with `publish_commit` on (external, tasks-repo): success line
  `<id> published <m> (the board; committed <short sha> on <branch>, not pushed)`; each refusal non-zero:

| Refusal | Message shape |
|---------|---------------|
| column outside board repo | `ledger publish <id>: <abs> is outside the board repo <btop> — publish_commit commits only inside it; nothing written` |
| untracked / ignored column | `ledger publish <id>: <abs> is not tracked in the board repo — commit it once by hand; nothing written` |
| filter attribute on the column | `ledger publish <id>: <abs> has a git filter (<name>) — a filter runs a program on commit; remove the attribute or leave publish_commit off; nothing written` |
| dirty column (unstaged or staged) | `ledger publish <id>: <abs> has uncommitted changes (<porcelain XY>) — commit or discard them first; nothing written` |
| sequencer in progress | `ledger publish <id>: the board repo has a <merge\|rebase\|cherry-pick\|revert> in progress — finish it first; nothing written` |
| detached HEAD | `ledger publish <id>: the board repo's HEAD is detached — check out a branch; nothing written` |
| path mismatch after mark | `ledger publish <id>: --mark wrote <p1>, located <p2> — nothing committed or recorded; check both files by hand` → touches neither file, die |
| nothing to commit (not a refusal) | exit 0, `<id> published <m> (the board; nothing to commit — the heading already showed it)`; `published` recorded |
| commit failed | `ledger publish <id>: git commit failed in <btop>: <git's last line> — the mark is rolled back; publish again once fixed` |

## Implementation Approach
1. **Locate before writing.** `--locate` shares `item_column()` with `--mark`, so the guarded path and the
   marked path come from one resolution; publish additionally checks the `path:` line `--mark` prints equals
   the located path (FR-004 "take the path from `--mark`").
2. **Guards run before `--mark`, in a cheap-to-expensive order**: inside `btop` (string prefix on physical
   paths, then `git ls-files --error-unmatch`) → sequencer state (`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute
   --git-path MERGE_HEAD|rebase-merge|rebase-apply|CHERRY_PICK_HEAD|REVERT_HEAD`) → detached HEAD
   (`git symbolic-ref -q --short HEAD`) → filter attribute (`git check-attr filter -- <abs>` value not
   `unspecified`: a clean/process filter runs a program on commit that no `GIT_CONFIG_*` pin reaches, spec D5)
   → dirty (`git status --porcelain=v1 -- <abs>` non-empty).
   Every git call is `git -C "$btop"`; the path is never passed to a git outside `btop`.
3. **One lock** (spec D8, FR-006; `$DIR/.publish.lock`, the `claim_lock` mkdir pattern, stale after one
   minute) spans locate → commit, so two publishes on the same column cannot sweep or roll back each other's
   marker. `$DIR` is the per-board ledger dir (`board-lib.sh:91-93`), shared by every code repo the board
   feeds. Taken only when `publish_commit` is on — today's path is untouched. Its EXIT trap also removes `$T`
   (the arm's temp file), so a guard's `die` leaves no temp file; `claim_lock`'s trap (`ledger.sh:362`) lives in
   another arm and is not clobbered.
4. **Commit** `git -C "$btop" -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -m "board: $ID ${M:-no marker}" -- "$abs"`.
   The pathspec IS git's `--only` mode (git-commit(1): the default when paths are given), so `--only` is not
   spelled and is not a mutation target; the pathspec is. The commit runs under `hef_git_neutral`
   (`ledger.sh:268`, `lane-lib.sh:116`): `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false` stay pinned —
   the board repo's hooks are **not run**, by the project's security invariant (`ledger.sh` is in
   `sandbox.excludedCommands`, `hefesto-setup.sh:15`/`:140`, and `publish` is lane-allowlisted, `:127`; an
   unpinned hook would be a lane-planted program run unsandboxed). `gpg.program` runs a program for the same
   reason, so signing is off for this commit (spec D5). Never unset a pinned key, never `push`, never
   `checkout -b`/`switch`. Precondition: the ledger process has a git identity.
5. **Nothing to commit.** After the mark, `git -C "$btop" diff --quiet HEAD -- "$abs"` true (the heading
   already showed the marker) → skip the commit, re-hash, record `published`, print the "nothing to commit"
   line. Without this a `git commit` exits 1 ("nothing to commit"), the rollback runs, and every pass retries
   forever.
6. **Rollback** on commit failure: `git -C "$btop" checkout -q HEAD -- "$abs"` (safe: the guard proved the
   file equalled HEAD before the mark, and the lock kept other publishes out), then die with git's reason.
   The re-hash and `published` are not reached → the next pass retries from a clean file.
7. **In-repo / github**: `publish_commit` true on an in-repo board prints
   `<id> publish: publish_commit applies to an external board only — not committed` after today's output;
   github-project ignores it.
8. **Path mismatch** between `--mark`'s `path:` line and the located path: touch nothing (rolling back the
   located path could discard a change made through the other path), die naming both, record nothing.
9. DONE (`not marked`): no commit, `published` recorded as today.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: one column resolution for `--mark` and `--locate`
**File:** `hooks/board-mark.sh` (new; `mark_item` moved from `status-board.sh:257–290`), `hooks/status-board.sh` (load `:41`, parse `:51`, dispatch `:602`, refusal `:608`)
**Intent:** the guarded path and the marked path cannot diverge.

```bash
item_column() { # $1 id → "<col>\t<abs resolved path>" | "done\t-" ; dies when absent
  local col f
  for col in todo doing backlog 'done'; do
    f="$TROOT/$(col "$col")"; [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    awk -v h="$ITEM_HEADING" -v id="$1" '…same match as :268…' "$f" || continue
    [ "$col" = 'done' ] && { printf 'done\t-\n'; return 0; }
    f=$(readlink -f "$f" 2>/dev/null || resolve_link "$f") || die "status-board: cannot resolve $f"
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$col" "$f"; return 0
  done
  die "status-board --mark $1: no such item in …"
}
# mark_item: loc=$(item_column "$1") || exit 1; done → "not marked"; else rewrite "${loc#*	}", then
#   echo "marked $1 $2 in $(col "${loc%%	*}")"; echo "path: ${loc#*	}"
```
**Why this shape:** today's resolution at `:274` happens after the DONE check; keeping that order keeps
the DONE message byte-identical.

### Sketch 2: the guards
**File:** `hooks/ledger-publish.sh` (new)
**Intent:** every refusal happens before a byte is written, with the evidence in the message.

```bash
publish_guard() { # $1 id, $2 btop, $3 abs → 0, or die
  case "$3/" in "$2"/*) ;; *) die "ledger publish $1: $3 is outside the board repo $2 — …; nothing written" ;; esac
  git -C "$2" ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$3" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ledger publish $1: $3 is not tracked …"
  local g s; for s in MERGE_HEAD:merge rebase-merge:rebase rebase-apply:rebase CHERRY_PICK_HEAD:cherry-pick REVERT_HEAD:revert; do
    g=$(git -C "$2" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path "${s%%:*}") || die "…cannot read the board repo's git dir"
    [ ! -e "$g" ] || die "ledger publish $1: the board repo has a ${s#*:} in progress — finish it first; nothing written"
  done
  git -C "$2" symbolic-ref -q --short HEAD >/dev/null || die "ledger publish $1: the board repo's HEAD is detached …"
  s=$(git -C "$2" check-attr filter -- "$3") || die "…git check-attr failed"; s=${s##*: }
  [ "$s" = unspecified ] || die "ledger publish $1: $3 has a git filter ($s) — …; nothing written"
  s=$(git -C "$2" status --porcelain=v1 -- "$3") || die "…git status failed"
  [ -z "$s" ] || die "ledger publish $1: $3 has uncommitted changes (${s:0:2}) — commit or discard them first; nothing written"
}
```
**Why this shape:** cites the five guards of the item; the `case` runs before any git call so a column
outside the repo never reaches git (spec US4 negative).

### Sketch 3: commit or roll back
**File:** `hooks/ledger-publish.sh` (new)

```bash
publish_commit_file() { # $1 id, $2 marker, $3 btop, $4 abs → "<sha12> on <branch>", or rollback + die
  local out br
  git -C "$3" diff --quiet HEAD -- "$4" && { echo "nothing"; return 0; }   # mark was a no-op: no commit, no rollback loop
  # hef_git_neutral already pinned hooksPath/fsmonitor for this process; never unset them here (spec D5)
  if ! out=$(git -C "$3" -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -m "board: $1 ${2:-no marker}" -- "$4" 2>&1); then
    git -C "$3" checkout -q HEAD -- "$4" 2>/dev/null || die "ledger publish $1: commit failed AND rollback of $4 failed — restore it by hand"
    die "ledger publish $1: git commit failed in $3: $(tail -n1 <<<"$out") — the mark is rolled back; publish again once fixed"
  fi
  br=$(git -C "$3" symbolic-ref --short HEAD); echo "$(git -C "$3" rev-parse --short=12 HEAD) on $br"
}
```

**File:** `hooks/ledger.sh` (modify at `:814–823`)

```bash
tasks-repo)
  …hash check as today (:815–818)…   # publish_lock's EXIT trap removes "$T" too
  if publish_commit_on; then BT=$(jq -r .board_top <<<"$BCTX"); publish_lock "$T"

    P=$(sed -n 's/^path: //p' <<<"$MARKED"); [ "$P" = "${LOC#*	}" ] || die "ledger publish $ID: --mark wrote $P, located ${LOC#*	} — nothing committed or recorded; …"   # touches neither file
    CM=$(publish_commit_file "$ID" "$M" "$BT" "$P") || { rm -f "$T"; exit 1; }
  fi

```
`publish_commit_on` = `is_external && [ "$(cfgp '.orchestrate.publish_commit // false')" = true ]`; on an
in-repo board with the flag true, the arm prints the "external board only" line. `publish_unlock` runs on
the EXIT trap (as `claim_lock` does, `ledger.sh:362`).

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Principle 1** (payload not under `.claude/`): the new file is `hooks/ledger-publish.sh` at the root payload.
- [x] **Principle 2** (namespaced commands): no new command; `ledger.sh` subcommand unchanged.
- [x] **Principle 3** (mutation-tested guards, tool-level assertions): each guard has a mutation (below); tests
  assert on git state (`git log`, `rev-parse HEAD`, sha256 of the file), not on model output. The failed-commit
  injector is a missing identity, which still fails under `hef_git_neutral` (a pre-commit hook would not run,
  so it could not make M8 go red); no mutation targets `--only`, which a pathspec commit already implies.
- [x] **Principle 4** (zero-install): bash, git, jq — already required. `--path-format=absolute` needs git ≥ 2.31
  (stock macOS git 2.39 complies); stated in docs.
- [x] **Principle 5** (fail loudly): every refusal is `die` non-zero with path/state; `--locate` dies on a missing
  item, never prints a sentinel at exit 0 (`done\t-` is a real answer the caller branches on, matching `--mark`'s own DONE handling).

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| A commit sweeps a person's edit | lost or mis-attributed work | dirty guard before mark + `-- <path>` pathspec + lock |
| Concurrent publishes on one column | marker swept or rolled back | `$DIR/.publish.lock` spans locate→commit |
| Commit fails after the mark | stuck "changed since claim" | rollback to HEAD before re-hash; `published` not written |
| No git identity for the ledger process | commit fails every pass | `ledger.sh` runs outside the lane sandbox (`sandbox.excludedCommands`), so sandbox write access is NOT the issue; fails closed through the rollback with git's reason; docs state the identity precondition |
| Board-repo hooks or signer run unsandboxed | a lane-planted program executed | the commit keeps `hef_git_neutral`'s pins and adds `commit.gpgsign=false` (spec D5); a test proves a failing `pre-commit` does not run |
| Pushing to main | an unreviewed board commit on a remote | never pushed; output says "not pushed"; docs state the branch expectation |
| ledger.sh / status-board.sh file length | the commit gate blocks a newly-crossed 500 (`quality-before-commit.sh:226`) | `ledger.sh` (721 code lines, already over) only calls the new `ledger-publish.sh`; `status-board.sh` (494) LOSES `mark_item` to `board-mark.sh`, so its code lines go down — measured with `code_lines` before commit |
| A new mandatory sibling breaks the mutation dirs | dozens of red smoke tests unrelated to the change | every dir that copies `ledger.sh`/`status-board.sh` gains the two symlinks (Affected Files) |

Mutations (SC-005), each must turn the suite red: (M1) drop the `case` outside-repo check; (M2) drop the
`ls-files` tracked check; (M3) drop the sequencer loop; (M4) drop the detached-HEAD check; (M5) drop the dirty
check; (M6) drop the `-- "$abs"` pathspec (commits what else is staged — the other-file-staged case goes red); (M7) record `published` before the commit; (M8) remove
the rollback; (M9) re-hash before the commit; (M10) treat `"true"` (string) as on; (M11) skip the lock (asserted
by a held `.publish.lock` making publish wait then refuse); (M12) drop the `check-attr filter` check (the
filter fixture commits); (M13) drop the nothing-to-commit skip (the no-op publish exits non-zero / loops);
(M14) roll back the located path on a mismatch (the mismatch case finds a file changed).
